headline: NY governor vetoes bromate & Red 3 ban; Granarolo adopts Foreverland cocoa-free chocolate
summary: New York Governor Hochul vetoed the bill banning potassium bromate, Red No. 3 and propylparaben and requiring food-chemical disclosure, so bakery customers get a reprieve in New York, but California's ban and FDA's Red 3 revocation mean bromate-free improvers and natural colours should stay a sales priority.

Granarolo is putting Foreverland's carob-based cocoa-free Choruba into a lactose-free Yomo product, a sign cocoa alternatives are reaching mainstream European dairy; Belcolade should benchmark Choruba for fillings and coatings.
Puratos is investing millions in a new ingredient facility in Romania, expanding its Eastern European capacity.
New sourdough microbiology from traditional Inner Mongolian starters and a CSIRO precision-fermentation yeast host are early science worth tracking for the sourdough library and enzyme sourcing.

items.title: Cocoa-Free Chocolate Dairy: Granarolo Adds Foreverland Choruba to a Lactose-Free Yomo…
items.summary: Italian dairy group Granarolo is using Foreverland's Choruba, a carob-based cocoa-free chocolate alternative, in a lactose-free Yomo product.
items.why: A mainstream dairy launch with a cocoa-free chocolate ingredient shows cocoa alternatives moving into retail; Belcolade should benchmark Choruba and consider cocoa-free options for fillings and coatings.

items.title: Did Hochul veto the food additive ban? Yes: Red 3, potassium bromate and propylparaben stay legal in New York
items.summary: New York Governor Hochul vetoed the bill that would have banned Red No. 3, potassium bromate and propylparaben and required disclosure of food chemicals, so the additives stay legal in New York.
items.why: Bakery customers using potassium bromate or Red 3 avoid a New York deadline for now, but with California's ban and FDA's Red 3 revocation the direction is clear; keep bromate-free improver and natural-colour offers front and centre.

items.title: New York’s governor vetoed a ban on 3 food additives found in bagels, pizza and cereal
items.summary: Coverage of New York Governor Hochul's veto of a ban on Red 3, potassium bromate and propylparaben, additives found in bagels, pizza and cereal.
items.why: Duplicate of the New York veto story; bakers using bromate get a reprieve in NY, but should still plan reformulation given pressure in other states.

items.title: Puratos invests millions in new Romanian ingredient facility
items.summary: Puratos is investing millions in a new ingredient facility in Romania.
items.why: Puratos's own capacity expansion in Eastern Europe; useful context for the newsletter rather than an external opportunity.

items.title: Exploration of the microbial diversity and functional characteristics of traditional sourdough in Inner Mongolia
items.summary: Food Microbiology study of the microbial diversity and functional traits of traditional sourdoughs in Inner Mongolia (no abstract available).
items.why: New sourdough strains from traditional Chinese starters could enrich Puratos's sourdough library and Sapore range.

items.title: Hochul vetoes food chemical disclosures, bans
items.summary: News report that Governor Hochul vetoed New York's food chemical disclosure requirements and additive bans.
items.why: Removes an imminent New York requirement for bakery customers using bromate, Red 3 or propylparaben and for GRAS disclosure; monitor reintroduction next session.

items.title: NY Gov. Hochul vetoes food safety bill, citing potential costs
items.summary: Governor Hochul vetoed New York's food safety bill, citing potential costs.
items.why: Same NY veto: compliance pressure eases short-term for bakery and patisserie customers, but reformulation away from bromate and Red 3 remains prudent.

items.title: Chickpea-based gluten-free bread as a matrix for grape pomace valorisation: Phenolic composition and bioaccessibility
items.summary: Turkish researchers added up to 15% industrial grape pomace to chickpea gluten-free bread and wheat bread, boosting phenolics and their bioaccessibility.
items.why: Upcycled grape pomace as a functional, fibre- and polyphenol-rich bakery ingredient is worth tracking for gluten-free and health-positioned breads.

items.title: Natural pigments from blueberry processing by-products for clean-label cherry coloration: accelerated shelf-life and overall microbiological stability
items.summary: University of Salerno coloured decolorised cherries with an anthocyanin extract from blueberry processing waste and tested shelf-life in sugar and reduced-sugar syrups.
items.why: Natural, upcycled anthocyanin colour for candied cherries is relevant to Patisserie decorations and fruit fillings as synthetic dyes like Red 3 are phased out.

items.title: This Thanksgiving, Big Food thankful for vetoed food safety law
items.source: Center for Science in the Public Interest
items.summary: CSPI criticises Governor Hochul's veto of New York's food chemical safety and disclosure law.
items.why: Advocacy groups will keep pushing additive bans state by state; bakery customers should not treat the veto as the end of bromate and dye scrutiny.
entities: Center for Science in the Public Interest
